snapshot.voting_system_note: The English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026 (Royal Assent 29 April 2026, section 63 and Schedule 30) restored the supplementary vote for mayoral and PCC elections. Commencement: SI 2026/656 brought the change into force on 18 June 2026 for elections whose notice is published on or after that date. The 7 May 2026 mayoral elections were the last under first past the post; every contest below uses the supplementary vote.
snapshot.method_note: Methods are reported separately and are never blended into a single point estimate. Where methods disagree on the most likely winner the contest is reported as method-split. Party-level projections only until nominations close; candidate effects in mayoral contests are large and the bands are wide by design.
caveats: Projections are party level. Mayoral contests have strong candidate effects (independents and well known local figures routinely beat party baselines) which cannot be modelled before nominations close.

The supplementary vote transfer model is calibrated on three verified counts: Greater Manchester 2026 (the one Reform era SV contest, including its per-district second-preference table) and Lancashire's own 2016 and 2021 PCC elections. The Lancashire hypothetical uses county-specific parameters: higher transfer reach (its own contests ran 58 to 66 percent) and weaker left-bloc cohesion (Reform won the GM second-preference battle in the Lancashire-like boroughs of Wigan, Oldham, Rochdale, Tameside and Bury). Parameters still carry deliberately wide noise; SV counts never reveal transfers by source candidate, so splits are pooled estimates.
The GE swing method applies uniform national swing to a general election base; local and mayoral elections routinely deviate from national swing (differential turnout, local parties, incumbency).
Mansfield is forecast subject to its caveat: Nottinghamshire reorganisation may abolish the post, and the contest should be re-verified when nominations open.
No constituency level polling exists for any May 2027 mayoral contest as of generation; the first published poll for a contest supersedes these baselines (wire it in, per the Makerfield lesson).

methods.label: 2023 mayoral result + proportional swing
methods.description: The mayoralty's own 2023 first-preference result, with each party moved by the ratio of its national polling now (9 polls, fieldwork to 2026-10-26) to its approximate May 2023 level, clamped at x2.5. methods.label: May 2026 borough votes, rebased to the polls of the time

validation.note: Every method understated Labour's first round by a wide margin: a well known incumbent-adjacent candidate on a 25% turnout beat her party's national baseline decisively. That gap is the candidate effect these projections cannot see before nominations, and it is why the bands are wide. Of the methods, the general election base came closest; the borough votes as cast, with no national rebasing, did worst and put Reform ahead.

hypothetical_lancashire.label: Mayor of Lancashire (hypothetical)
hypothetical_lancashire.status_note: No Lancashire mayoral election has been ordered. Material published with the 28 October 2026 Budget lists Lancashire among the areas where the government is in the final stages of agreeing a mayoral strategic authority, and a first election is reported for May 2028, conditional on that deal concluding. This models a county-wide supplementary vote contest on today's numbers. It is not a forecast of the 2028 result, which is about 18 months away; it will be replaced by a real forecast once an election is ordered.
hypothetical_lancashire.election_target: May 2028 (reported, subject to the deal concluding; not yet ordered)

sv_overrides.rationale: Lancashire-specific calibration, verified 8 Aug 2026: its own SV contests show higher transfer reach (0.583 in 2016, 0.656 in 2021) than the global anchors, and GM 2026 per-district second preferences show weaker left-bloc cohesion in Lancashire-like boroughs (Reform won transfers in Wigan, Oldham, Rochdale, Tameside, Bury). See sv_calibration entries lancashire_pcc_2016/2021 and gm_2026. Other transfers as right bloc (29 Oct 2026): in current polls Other is mostly Restore Britain (4% where reported), whose voters are right bloc; splitting it 50/50 understated Reform transfers.

noise.rationale: Proportional, zero-sum error (29 Oct 2026). The additive 6-point error floored at zero gave small parties implausible ranges (Liberal Democrats 0 to 11% from a 3% centre). sd 0.25 keeps the two leading parties' p10 to p90 bands about as wide as the additive error (about 14 to 15 points); it is not yet calibrated on past county results.

methods.label: GE2024 base + national swing
methods.description: General election 2024 results across the fourteen Lancashire councils, the twelve districts plus Blackburn with Darwen and Blackpool (16 constituencies apportioned by live postcode share), moved by the uniform national swing to the latest Westminster poll average (9 polls, fieldwork to 2026-10-26).

base.source: GE2024 constituency results (DC), ONS postcode crosswalk

methods.label: Lancashire local signal (unitaries model), rebased to current polls
methods.description: The county's own most recent local votes, taken from our Lancashire unitaries forecast: each proposed ward's LCC May 2025 division result nudged by the district's 2025 to 2026 borough and by-election swing, Blackburn's May 2026 wards directly, and a Blackpool proxy; electorate-weighted across the fourteen councils. Carries the local Reform organisation and independent vote the GE base misses. Those votes were cast when the national poll average was Reform UK 26.1%, Labour 18.3%, Conservative 18.5%, Green Party 16.2% (13 polls, fieldwork 2026-04-23 to 2026-05-06); they are moved by uniform swing from that average to the latest one (9 polls, fieldwork to 2026-10-26).

caveats: No election has been ordered. The May 2028 date is reported from material published with the 28 October 2026 Budget and is conditional on a mayoral strategic authority being agreed; the Lancashire Combined County Authority is non mayoral until then.

Eighteen months out. National polling moved by more than ten points in the six months to October 2026 (Labour 18% in early May, 29% in late October), so read these as today's position, not a 2028 forecast.

The supplementary vote transfer calibration leans on the Greater Manchester by-election, a much more Labour leaning electorate than Lancashire. Same-bloc cohesion is set at 70% on both sides; the Greater Manchester pooled count is only reproducible with left cohesion above right (about 85% against 70% at equal reach), so this may slightly understate Labour's Green and Liberal Democrat transfers. Other, which in current polls is mostly Restore Britain, transfers as right bloc.
Candidate and turnout effects are not modelled. In the Greater Manchester backtest the GE method called the winner but understated the Labour first round by about ten points.
Turnout for a standalone mayoral contest would be low and uneven; neither base fully captures that.

sv_calibration.note: Supplementary vote transfer behaviour anchors, verified 8 August 2026 against the returning authorities. Derived parameters: transfer reach (share of eliminated candidates' votes that reach a finalist) was 60.8 percent in Greater Manchester 2026 (103,326 of 169,949; 66,623 exhausted) and 44.3 percent in London 2021 (276,863 of 624,585). Of transfers reaching the finalists in GM 2026, 56.2 percent went to the Labour finalist and 43.8 percent to the Reform UK finalist, despite the eliminated pool leaning right of centre (Restore Britain plus Conservative outweighed Green plus Liberal Democrats).

backtest.note: Inputs for the validation backtest. Every method is run with the national poll average from the fortnight before polling day, not today's polls, so the error is the one the method would have made at the time.

lancashire_pcc_2021.note: Con won 51.27-48.73. Eliminated pool LD 32,813 + Reform UK 17,926 (fringe-era Reform, 4.83pct: do NOT map onto 2026 Reform). Transfers derived from official first/final counts; OPCC publishes no exhausted breakdown.

lancashire_pcc_2016.note: Lab won. UKIP-era pool (UKIP 16.54pct + LD) split near-evenly Con/Lab: right-populist ballots did NOT break heavily Conservative in Lancashire.

gm_2026.district_signal: Official per-district table: Reform (Astley) WON second preferences in Wigan, Oldham, Rochdale, Tameside and Bury; Labour (Craig) dominated Manchester, Stockport, Trafford. Lancashire's geography resembles the former group, so pooled GM parameters lean Labour when applied to Lancashire.
